title: Microsoft Purview: retention based on last accessed date for SharePoint and OneDrive files
summary: Hold: the retention-policy automation entry omits required arguments and is not a complete command. The admin-opt-in default is also unsubstantiated: Microsoft announces automatic availability but does not explicitly establish the new control's default enforcement behavior.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes planned retention for each SharePoint or OneDrive item based on its last access by a user.
claims.quote: This creates the ability to apply Retention to each SharePoint or OneDrive item based on when it was last accessed by a user. #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.quote: Enable admins to apply retention policy or retention label in OneDrive and SharePoint for files that have not been accessed by anyone in the organization after a period of time.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row API
claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy; New-RetentionComplianceRule is the runnable automation equivalent for creating the general retention policy.
claims.quote:
New-RetentionCompliancePolicy
    [-Name] <String>

The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy.
| Mandatory: | True |
claims.fix: Replace the API call in front matter and the table with 'New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy-name> -SharePointLocation <site-url> -OneDriveLocation <onedrive-url>', keeping its existing docs URL. Add the qualifier 'Creates the policy object; creating a policy also requires New-RetentionComplianceRule.' The existing two bare cmdlets omit mandatory arguments; the separately checked rule reference also requires -Policy and, for its default parameter set, -Name. Do not present this general policy-creation call as configuring the undocumented last-accessed trigger.

claims.claim: An archive inactivity period entirely after July 2025 gives a more complete observation period but does not exclude files with older recorded dates.
claims.quote: For critical content, choose an inactivity period that falls entirely after July 2025. This provides a more complete observation period; it doesn't exclude files with older LADs.

claims.claim: The new Purview last-accessed control has an admin-opt-in default.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "last accessed" "default"; read roadmap record, MC999442, /purview/retention and /purview/create-retention-policies. MC999442 states automatic availability, but no source explicitly states the new control's default enforcement.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'unknown'. Preserve the attributed statement that MC999442 says the feature will be available by default and roll out automatically, and add: 'Microsoft has not stated whether existing retention configurations change automatically.' For a feature that is itself a control, the standard requires explicit evidence that it enforces by default or restricts nothing until configured; automatic availability alone does not establish either.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist's retention-administrator permission review has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check who holds the Compliance Administrator role group and whether any retention administrator is limited by administrative units.' Table rows cover retention policies, archive policies and the last-accessed start option, but not administrator permissions.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Check who holds the Compliance Administrator role group and whether any retention administrator is limited by administrative units.' The verified role and administrative-unit facts can remain in Scope; do not add a control row as part of this correction.
